question: A junction diode is used in a half-wave rectifier. Explain how the depletion region behaviour during alternate half-cycles produces a unidirectional output.

options.A:
Forward-biased half-cycle
The barrier potential decreases and depletion region narrows, so majority carriers cross the junction and current flows through the load.
Reverse-biased half-cycle
The barrier increases and depletion region widens, so almost no current flows. Thus output occurs during alternate half-cycles in one direction and is pulsating DC.
options.B:
Forward-biased half-cycle
The depletion region widens and blocks all current.
Reverse-biased half-cycle
The depletion region narrows and allows large current, so output is alternating.
options.C:
Both half-cycles
The depletion region remains unchanged, so the diode passes identical current in both directions and produces AC output.
options.D:
Reverse-biased half-cycle
Majority carriers cross the widened depletion layer easily, giving a larger current than forward bias.
